section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the concept of "you and your sons shall live on the leftover" relates to making oneself like remnants, which draws down the encompassing lights (makifim) that are above the chain of descent, specifically through self-nullification.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter in more detail
will be understood according to what is stated in Likkutei Torah22
that the matter of "you and your sons shall live on the leftover" is in the manner of what our sages said23
on the verse24
"for the remnant of His inheritance,"
for one who makes himself like remnants.
And it is explained there25,
that "remnants" are the encompassing lights that are above the chain of descent.
For the light that is drawn down into the worlds
(in the internal aspect)
is only an illumination,
while the essence of the light
(the encompassing lights)
remains above,
as remnants.
And in order to draw down the encompassing lights,
it is through self-nullification.
And this is "for one who makes himself like remnants,"
for by making himself like remnants literally,
self-nullification,
specifically through this he draws down the encompassing lights,
the remnants.
For when his service is in the category of existence,
even when the service is at the ultimate level of elevation,
the drawing down that comes through it is light that belongs to the chain of descent
(existence),
and in order to draw down the remnants from above
(which are above the category of existence)
it is specifically through self-nullification.
[And as is also explained in Torah Or26
on the verse27
"The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool; which house... and to this one I will look: to the poor and broken-spirited,"
that the drawing down that comes through heaven and earth, which are Torah
(heaven)
and mitzvos
(earth)
is internal light,
and in order to draw down the encompassing lights,
"which house,"
for "house" is an encompassing light
(and within the encompassing lights themselves, the distant encompassing light),
it is through self-nullification,
"poor and broken-spirited."]
And it is explained in Likkutei Torah there,
that this is what our sages said28
on the verse "and you and your sons shall live on the leftover until the dead are revived,"
that "leftover" is what remains above in the category of encompassing light,
and within the encompassing lights themselves it is the distant encompassing light,
Atik
(for Arich is the near encompassing light and Atik is the distant encompassing light29),
and this is "you shall live on the leftover until the dead are revived,"
for the revival of the dead is through the dew that drips from Atik30.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contrasts two levels: serving through Torah and mitzvos even without love and fear draws the near encompassing light (Arich), while feeling bitter over being an empty vessel brings self-nullification and draws the distant encompassing light (Atik).
section.t: And this is the superiority of the matter of "you shall live on the leftover" that comes through the bitterness of being an empty vessel
(the second interpretation of "do not diminish from empty vessels")
over the matter of "you shall live on the leftover" that comes through engaging in Torah and mitzvos even though he has no love and fear
(the first interpretation of "do not diminish from empty vessels"),
for the advantage
(leftover)
in this—that he engages in Torah and mitzvos even when he has no love and fear—is that then his fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos is connected with the power of self-sacrifice,
for the matter of self-sacrifice stems from the essence of the soul, which is above the revealed faculties
(love and fear).
But nevertheless,
since through the engagement in Torah and mitzvos
(even when the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos is through remembering the matter of his self-sacrifice to G-d)
he is not nullified from his existence
[for the fact that he fulfills Torah and mitzvos depends on his will,
the will
(existence)
of the person31],
the revelation of the essence of the soul in this is only as it relates to the revealed faculties
[for by remembering the matter of his self-sacrifice to G-d, which stems from the essence of the soul,
his will in Torah and mitzvos is with great force].
Therefore,
also the drawing down that is drawn from above through this
is the light that is above the chain of descent as it relates to the chain of descent,
which in general is the near encompassing light,
Arich.
And the advantage that is made through the feeling and bitterness of being an empty vessel,
since through this he is nullified from his existence,
through this is drawn the revelation of the essence of the soul as it is above relation to the revealed faculties.
And likewise is it regarding the drawing down that is drawn from above through this,
for by feeling in himself that he is an empty vessel with no virtue and is like remnants in his eyes
(a superfluous thing,
leftover),
the matter of "you shall live on the leftover" is that through this there is a drawing down of the distant encompassing light,
Atik32.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies how the "leftover" (the distant encompassing light of Atik) can give life to internal faculties like love and fear, explaining that the soul of Israel inherently contains even the highest levels of "wondrous" and "distant."
section.t: And we need to understand what is stated: "you and your sons shall live on the leftover,"
that also the love and fear of the soul
(your sons)
shall live on the leftover,
for seemingly,
since "leftover" is an encompassing light,
and especially according to the interpretation that "leftover" is the distant encompassing light,
how can vitality from it be drawn down to the internal faculties
(love and fear)?
And this can be explained according to what the Rebbe
(the Rebbe Rashab)
of blessed memory, the birthday owner, said in his maamar beginning with "Ki"33
"For this commandment which I command you today, it is not wondrous for you nor is it distant from you"34
(in his book of maamarim that is now being prepared for print35),
that the two terms "wondrous" and "distant" correspond to Atik and Arich.
For "wondrous"
[which is a term of separation and distinction]
is in Atik,
which is removed and separated from the chain of descent,
and "distant" is in Arich,
for the term "distant" indicates that it has a relation to the thing from which it is distant,
as in "I said, 'I will become wise,' but it was distant from me"36,
for this that "I said, 'I will become wise'" is because wisdom relates to him,
only that it is distant from him37.
And it is explained there,
that what is written "for this commandment... it is not wondrous for you...,"
specifically "for you,"
is
because since the mitzvos are the Supernal Will,
a will that is above reason,
they are in the category of wondrous and distant38.
And all the more so the mitzvah of teshuvah
(for "this commandment" refers to the mitzvah of teshuvah,
as the Ramban and several commentators say39)
which is above the will of the mitzvos
[and as is explained in many places40,
that this—that through teshuvah all blemishes are filled—is because teshuvah reaches the Ein Sof, the Master of Will
(which is above the will of the mitzvos),
to the extent that it reaches the very Essence41,
and this is what is written "for this commandment which I command you,"
"I am that I am"42]
which is certainly in the category of wondrous and distant.
For lower teshuvah is in the category of distant, and higher teshuvah is in the category of wondrous.
Because lower teshuvah is in the encompassing light of Chayah,
the near encompassing light.
And also the drawing down from above that is drawn through lower teshuvah is the encompassing light of direct light that has a relation to the internal,
which in general is Arich.
And higher teshuvah is in the encompassing light of Yechidah,
the distant encompassing light.
And also the drawing down from above that is drawn through this is the encompassing light of returning light that is above relation to the internal,
which in general is Atik.
And what is written "it is not wondrous for you nor is it distant from you"
is specifically "for you,"
for the souls of Israel.
For the souls of Israel contain everything,
and also from above they are given everything,
and therefore this is not wondrous or distant from them.
